A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 21-page versions of SpectralGCD, including Appendices A-I. Their text, equations, tables, and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results on six datasets, ablations, timing measurements, and supplementary linear-probing and retrieval experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark evaluation in Table 1 and experimental analyses throughout the appendices.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1-4.3 retain the same cross-modal representation, spectral filtering, and forward/reverse distillation. The added appendix statements disclose implementation and ablation details without establishing a change to the underlying method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six GCD benchmarks and retain the dictionary, class-imbalance, linear-probing, and retrieval scenarios. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership and variants remain unchanged across the corresponding comparisons, including SimGCD, GET, and TextGCD. Appendix B.2 clarifies the existing SimGCD cross-modal variant rather than introducing another comparator.

E3.justification: Dataset splits and sample counts in Table 8, evaluation metrics, model configurations, and training settings remain unchanged, including 200 epochs and batch size 128. Appendix B.2 supplies previously unstated ablation controls without revising a previously stated setting.

E4.justification: The same feature-input, distillation, threshold, dictionary, teacher, encoder-tuning, imbalance, and representation analyses appear in both versions. The expanded feature-ablation description adds no tested condition or analytical result.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three seeds, report benchmark means and standard deviations in Table 7, and provide Spearman variability and p-values in Table 11. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted findings, and qualitative outcomes are retained throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 still reports SpectralGCD All accuracy of 79.2 on CUB and 89.1 on Stanford Cars, and Table 9's feature-ablation results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, sufficient-representation assumption, spectral derivation, and Equations 1-12 remain unchanged. Section 3 changes the prose loss subscripts from con to c to match Equation 1; this is notation consistency rather than revised mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about semantic representations, spectral filtering, distillation, discovery accuracy, and computational efficiency. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning Old/New performance, teacher alignment, dictionary quality, and text-encoder drift remain unchanged, as do the teacher and dictionary coverage limitations in Section 6. The added passages primarily explain implementation choices for existing experiments.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly states that Old class names are appended after spectral filtering. Appendix B.2 clarifies that the image-feature variant retains filtering and both distillation losses while changing only classifier input, and that SimGCD's cross-modal variant filters using the student. These are useful additional reproducibility details for retained experiments.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, related-work discussion, and positioning against earlier GCD and multimodal approaches are unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds localized explanations in Appendices A and B.2, makes the contrastive-loss notation consistent in Section 3, and adds a Figure 3 cross-reference. The overall narrative and section ordering remain intact.

P2.justification: All 18 tables and nine figures retain their content and captions. Added prose causes limited appendix layout shifts, including repositioning Figure 8 and Table 15 and moving the Appendix C opening from page 16 to page 17.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility and clarity by specifying dictionary augmentation and the construction of existing feature-input ablations in Appendices A and B.2. The notation correction provides another small benefit. These resolve limited documentation ambiguities while leaving the empirical evidence and conclusions unchanged.
